title: Cell signaling and receptors (general); Hormones and the endocrine system
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: HO08b#t2 term and clue written for the game; HO08b#t3 term and clue written for the game; HO02a#t4 term and clue written for the game; HO02a#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: HO02a#N.3b, HO08b#N.6, HO02a#N.11, HO08b#N.11, HO08b#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Adenylyl cyclase
items.clue: Effector enzyme that converts ATP to cAMP.

items.label: Phosphodiesterase
items.clue: Enzyme that breaks down cAMP, switching the signal off.

items.label: Nervous system
items.clue: Sends electrical impulses to specific cells; acts within milliseconds.

items.label: Endocrine gland
items.clue: Ductless organ that secretes its chemical product directly into the blood.

questions.stem: A hormone released into the blood by a gland affects only some of the body's cell types. Which statement best explains why only these cell types respond to it?

options.text: The gland sends the hormone straight to its target cells, so other cell types do not receive it.
The cell types that respond let the hormone in, and a hormone acts on a cell only from inside it.
The cell types that respond have receptors that recognize the hormone; other cell types lack them.
Cells close to the gland receive enough hormone to respond, but cells far away get too little.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly describes the events after epinephrine (adrenaline) binds to its receptor on a liver cell?

options.text: Epinephrine enters the liver cell and directly activates the enzymes that break down glycogen into glucose.
cAMP is released from the liver cell into the blood as a second messenger that acts on other liver cells.
A G protein is activated, adenylyl cyclase converts ATP to cAMP, and cAMP activates kinases that switch on glycogen breakdown.
The activated G protein converts ATP into cAMP, and the cAMP then breaks glycogen down directly into glucose.

questions.explanation: The activated G protein switches on adenylyl cyclase, cAMP activates protein kinases, and the phosphorylated enzymes break down glycogen.

questions.stem: In humans, cells of the pituitary gland at the base of the brain release human growth hormone, and target cells in many tissues respond, leading to growth. Which flowchart best represents how this signal reaches and affects its target cells?

options.text: Pituitary cell → blood → cells all over the body → every cell reached responds → growth
Pituitary cell → one vessel to target tissue alone → target cells respond → growth
Pituitary cell → nerve impulse down the spinal cord → target cells respond → growth
Pituitary cell → blood → cells all over the body → only cells with receptors respond → growth

questions.stem: A mutation changes the intracellular domain of a G protein-coupled receptor so that it activates its G protein whether or not ligand is bound. The ligand-binding domain is unchanged. What is predicted?

options.text: No response at all, because a mutated receptor can no longer bind its ligand.
A response only when extra ligand is added, to make up for the mutation.
The pathway is active even with no ligand bound, so the response continues all the time.
No change, because only mutations in the ligand-binding domain affect signalling.

questions.explanation: The G protein is activated whether or not ligand is present, so everything downstream stays switched on.

questions.stem: Drug Z inhibits phosphodiesterase, the enzyme that breaks down cAMP. Liver cells treated with Z are given a short pulse of epinephrine, which is then washed away. Compared with untreated cells, what is predicted?

options.text: Glycogen breakdown stops the moment epinephrine is washed away, so Z makes no difference.
No glycogen breakdown at all, because Z blocks the epinephrine receptor.
cAMP leaves the treated cells and activates glycogen breakdown in neighbouring cells.
cAMP stays high for longer, so glycogen breakdown continues for longer.

questions.explanation: The pathway is switched on as normal, but its off-switch is blocked. cAMP lingers, kinases stay active and glycogen breakdown is prolonged.
